methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $299M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Electra, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sandeep Nijhawan and Quoc Pham, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in frontier-tech energy infrastructure. The peer set includes KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, all at Series C stage with valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's $299M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding $568M. Peer-median analysis draws on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, producing a median valuation of $1.0B (with a range of $700M to $3.0B). The peer-median approach reflects elevated valuations in the climate-tech sector during the funding period represented by these comps.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $483M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $784M. The 130% spread between low and high estimates reflects meaningful uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation multiples and the heterogeneity of peer-company technology maturity and capital requirements. Key sensitivities include comparable company selection—particularly the weighting of the $3.0B outlier (KoBold Metals)—and whether Electra's technology trajectory and market timing justify peer-level or sub-peer positioning within the climate-energy landscape.
